This page covers installing Fiordland on a PC. The short version is in the [https://fiordlandlinux.org/docs/install/ official install guide]; this page collects extra details and hardware notes.

== Requirements ==
* 64-bit x86 PC (x86_64). UEFI recommended, legacy BIOS works too.
* 4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB or more recommended.
* 30 GB disk minimum. The installer erases the disk you pick.
* A USB stick of 4 GB or more.

== Make the USB stick ==
# Download the ISO from the [https://fiordlandlinux.org website].
# Check it: the SHA-256 is shown on the download page. On Linux: <code>sha256sum fiordland-*.iso</code>.
# Write it:
#* Windows: [https://rufus.ie Rufus] (pick ''DD image mode'' if asked) or [https://etcher.balena.io balenaEtcher].
#* macOS: balenaEtcher.
#* Linux: <code>sudo dd if=fiordland-*.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress oflag=sync</code> (replace <code>sdX</code> with the USB stick, not your disk).

== Boot it ==
* Restart and open the boot menu. The key is usually F12, F11, F8, Esc or F2 (it often shows briefly on screen).
* Turn off '''Secure Boot''' in the firmware settings. Fiordland's boot files are not signed yet.
* On some laptops you also need to switch the SATA mode from RAID/Intel RST to AHCI, or the disk will not show up. Back up Windows first if you dual boot.

== The installer ==
The live session starts in KDE Plasma and opens the installer. You can also try the system first and start '''Install Fiordland''' from the menu later.

You pick language, keyboard, timezone, the disk, your account, and a desktop. On the review page you can change the graphics driver and the kernel. The install takes 5 to 20 minutes depending on your internet speed, since packages are downloaded fresh.

== After installing ==
* Remove the USB stick when the computer restarts.
* Read [[tawaki]] to install apps.
* Run <code>tawaki update</code> once a week or so.

== Dual boot ==
On a computer that starts in UEFI mode, the disk step offers '''Install alongside Windows'''. It shrinks the Windows partition (nothing is deleted) and you choose how much space Fiordland gets. Free space on the disk is offered too. When the computer starts, the GRUB menu lists both Fiordland and Windows.

Before you start, in Windows:
* Back up your important files.
* Turn off '''Fast Startup''' (Control Panel, Power Options, Choose what the power buttons do) and shut down fully.
* Turn off '''BitLocker''' or '''Device encryption''' for the Windows drive. Encrypted partitions cannot be shrunk.

Windows runs a disk check the first time it starts after the shrink. This is normal.

Installing on a second disk also works: pick that disk and choose '''Erase the disk'''. GRUB adds Windows from the other disk to its menu.

Computers that start in legacy BIOS mode, and disks with the old MBR layout, cannot use '''Install alongside Windows'''. Use '''Choose partitions''' instead.

== Choose partitions ==
For other systems, other Linux installs, or your own layout, pick '''Choose partitions''' on the disk step:
* '''Install Fiordland on''': any partition of 16 GB or more. Only this partition is formatted (Btrfs).
* '''Boot files go on''' (UEFI): an existing FAT32 EFI system partition. It is kept as it is; Fiordland adds its own folder.
* '''Partition editor''' opens KDE Partition Manager to shrink, delete or create partitions. The list updates when you close it.

A UEFI disk without an EFI system partition needs one first: 512 MB, FAT32, with the ''boot'' and ''esp'' flags. A BIOS computer with a GPT disk needs a 1 MB partition with the ''bios_grub'' flag. On BIOS, GRUB is written to the start of the disk and lists the other systems it finds.
